plurals.item: Imported %1$d trigger area, disabled until you review it
Imported %1$d trigger areas, disabled until you review them

resources.string: A trigger area is a zone on screen you tap during a game; each tap sends taps to the target points you configured. It is not a recording.
The zone and its target points are removed. If it is on screen right now it disappears immediately.
Off makes the zone fully transparent; it still reacts to taps.
Nothing on screen. Triggers bound to an app appear when that app is in front; others when you arm them.
Trigger areas draw a small overlay and inject taps through the accessibility service – no root, no “draw over other apps” permission. Each item below is checked live; nothing is assumed.
Your explicit agreement to the current disclosure is required before the service may show trigger zones and inject taps in other apps. If you agreed to an earlier version, read and agree again.
Turn on “MacroAndroid” under Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps.
Android may show “Restricted setting” for side-loaded apps: open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings first.
Android has not bound the service yet. Toggle it off and on in Accessibility settings if this persists.
The bound service does not report gesture support. Re-enable the service after updating the app.
Tap empty space to add a target point. Drag points and the trigger zone; drag its corner to resize. Shaded bands are system bars.
Test finished – all target taps were injected

Targets are tapped one after another with the delay set on each point.
All enabled targets go down together as one multi-finger gesture (genuine simultaneous contacts, max 10). Per-point delays are ignored.
Wait this long after your press before the first target is tapped. 0 reacts immediately.
Shows the area and targets full-screen over the game so you can drag them into place. Tap Done there to save.
